problem.claim: Language-model benchmarks can produce contradictory rankings, complicating model selection and comparison.

gap.claim: Direct-evaluation rankings are reported to have little external validity across benchmarks, motivating a complementary comparison perspective.

contributions.claim: Introduces train-before-test: identical benchmark-specific fine-tuning precedes evaluation to compare model potential.
Evaluates model potential across 24 benchmarks and 61 models.
Reports consistent cross-benchmark model-potential rankings, restored perplexity–downstream-performance association, and an essentially rank-one model-score matrix.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish model-potential comparison through identical pre-evaluation fine-tuning from out-of-the-box direct evaluation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that train-before-test rankings show remarkable consistency across all evaluated benchmarks.
Authors report that model-potential rankings transfer across benchmarks, unlike traditional direct-evaluation rankings, which show little external validity.
Authors report that pre-finetuning base-model perplexity predicts post-finetuning downstream performance and that the resulting score matrix is essentially rank one.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contradictory benchmark rankings hinder model selection and comparison.
The paper compares achievable model performance by applying identical benchmark-specific fine-tuning before testing.
The authors report highly consistent rankings and stronger transfer between benchmarks under train-before-test.
The authors report restored perplexity predictiveness and an essentially rank-one score matrix, associating consistency with a latent factor and inherent potential rather than fine-tuning artifacts.
Direct evaluation is retained for deployment-ready performance, while train-before-test is framed as complementary for post-adaptation potential.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates deployment-ready performance under direct evaluation from achievable post-adaptation performance under train-before-test.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its evaluation target explicit when different protocols answer different practical questions.
lessons.application: Define whether each experiment measures current usability or post-adaptation potential, and align the comparison protocol with that target.
lessons.exception: This separation is unsuitable when the research question concerns only unadapted deployment behavior.

source_observation.claim: The authors connect cross-benchmark ranking consistency with perplexity predictiveness and a rank-one score structure.

lessons.interpretation: Linking headline ranking results to an independent proxy and compact structural summary can support a more explanatory narrative.
lessons.application: When reporting ranking stability, add a prespecified proxy or low-dimensional analysis that tests whether the pattern reflects a shared factor.
lessons.exception: Such analyses may mislead when the proxy or factor model is not justified for the task family.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 24 benchmarks, 61 models, fine-tuning data or procedures, statistical criteria, or effect sizes.
The basis for the claim that direct rankings have little external validity and the meaning of “essentially rank one” are not detailed.
The abstract does not establish whether train-before-test is operationally feasible or preferable for particular deployment settings.
